title: Fluid column resizing and robust row virtualization measurements
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our table component shows visual/interaction glitches when users perform rapid column resize gestures while scrolling large virtualized datasets. Resizing snaps unpredictably, header-to-body alignment can drift when row heights are measured lazily, and density toggles reset column widths unexpectedly.

Goal: Design a resilient column resizing UX that feels 'fluid' across density modes and preserves alignment with virtualized rows. Reduce layout jank during concurrent scroll/resize, provide clear affordances for exact and freeform resizing, and define token-level spacing rules so density switches are predictable. Deliver final specs, a small interaction prototype, and accessibility guidelines for keyboard and touch interactions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Column resize drag remains smooth without causing virtualized row re-measure thrash on large datasets (100k+ rows) across viewport sizes; 2) Header column edges visually align with rows after resize and during fast scrolling; 3) Density switch preserves user-adjusted column widths unless explicit 'reset to compact defaults' is chosen; 4) Keyboard resize (modifier + arrow) supported and documented for accessibility; 5) Edge cases documented: column groups, pinned columns, and column auto-size; 6) Hand-off-ready Figma frames and a short interaction gif attached; 7) Implementation notes for ENG to avoid forced reflow of entire table when measuring rows.
design_notes:
Explored three patterns: (A) measurement-first: precompute row heights for visible window then allow resizing; (B) decoupled-measure / deferred-apply: buffer resize deltas and apply after microtask to avoid synchronous reflows; (C) kernelized-resize: use transform-only visual handle while committing width on pointerup. We prefer (C) as primary with (B) as fallback for browsers without stable transforms for table layout. Define spacing tokens: table.gap-xs/md/lg mapped to density presets; column-handle-hitbox token to 12px. Use a 2-phase visual affordance: thin dragline while dragging, explicit width label at hover/drag for precise adjustments. For auto-size, present a double-click action that measures a sampled subset (first 200 visible rows) to avoid full-scan.

Trade-offs: (C) reduces reflow but requires careful commit logic to update column width state used by virtualizer; sampled auto-size may miss some tall cell exceptions but balances perf and accuracy.
usability_findings: Lab test (6 participants, mix of trackpad and mouse): users expected column width to persist across density changes; three participants double-clicked expecting auto-fit; touch users had trouble hitting narrow handles under compact density. Key insights: increase hit area, show width tooltip during drag, and add an explicit 'reset widths' affordance in the column menu. Accessibility check: screen reader announcement on column resize completed is required to convey state change.
engineer_feedback: ENG: prefer transform-only preview because it avoids layout thrash (ENG-2684)
ENG: virtualizer currently re-measures on any width change; need API to batch width commits (ENG-2712)
ENG: pinned columns require special handling because they render in a separate layer; propose mirrored commit event.
review_comments: PM Mateo Alvarez: favours preserving user widths across density toggles; ensure opt-in behavior if customers want compact defaults.
Design Lead Priya Rao: prefer the transform preview pattern, but add visual confirmation to reduce surprise.
Accessibility Lead Jacob Kim: add keyboard + aria-live announcement for final widths, and document touch target sizes.
QA Elena Park: add tests for resize while scrolling at 60fps and layout sanity checks after density change.
